corrections_summary: No status or year changes. One entry (dose 2) rests on a scanned FDA review whose quote cannot be verified; add or substitute the EPAR 2007 quote (same year, same status). Optionally flip product_in_model to null on the safety entries, since a human genetic model is neither dosed nor a proxy.
rule_questions: Does inherited human C5 deficiency (a natural genetic model, never dosed) count as 'the model the class relied on' in a preclinical-model atlas? The class demonstrably relied on it (EPAR expectation, exclusion criteria, mandatory vaccination). If it is disallowed, the safety model becomes BB5.1 mouse toxicology, silent on Neisseria, and by the ad-amyloid precedent (silence not holding = contra) safety 2007 flips from same to contra.

Rule 1 says a non-untested status needs a primary source that makes the comparison, but the cf-cftr house example scores a juxtaposed same (Ramsey 2011 patient data vs Van Goor 2009 cells) and v2 says comparison_stated must not change the status. Confirm juxtaposition is allowed; if not, engagement and efficacy same move from 2004 (Hillmen) to 2007 (FDA review / EPAR).
Are EMA EPAR scientific discussions acceptable primary sources? Rule 1 names only FDA label/review and registries; v2's model_filed field says 'FDA/EMA review'.

Efficacy silence: the safety question explicitly scores a model's silence, the efficacy question does not. C3-mediated extravascular hemolysis is an efficacy-limiting mechanism the chicken-RBC assay cannot see (no CD55-negative cells). Treated here as not contra because the model's actual prediction held; the brief should say whether un-modelled efficacy residuals ever count.

Scanned FDA reviews: can an OCR-read quote satisfy rule 2 ('verbatim') when the checker has no way to re-read it? Suggest requiring a text-layer backup source or an OCR transcript attached to the draft.
